photo.alt: THANKSGIVING: Filet Mignon + Lobster Tails, Brown-Butter Cauliflower Mash, Garlic-Butter Mushrooms, Asparagus + Chocolate Espresso Mousse

stepSections.title: Filet mignon
steps: Pat the filets dry and season both sides with salt and pepper. Keep the 220 g filet for Jake and the 180 g filet for Laine.

Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the filets for about 2–3 minutes per side, then briefly sear the edges. Reduce the heat, add a portion of the measured butter, and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks as they finish.
Check each filet in the center with an instant-read thermometer. Remove each when it reaches 145°F and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving. The smaller filet may finish first.

stepSections.title: Butter-broiled lobster tails
steps: Thaw frozen tails in the refrigerator. With kitchen shears, split each top shell lengthwise, stopping at the tail fan. Loosen the meat and lift it over the shell, leaving it attached at the base.
Preheat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below the element. Set the tails on a broiler-safe pan and brush the exposed meat with melted butter.
Broil until pearly and opaque throughout and the thickest part reaches 145°F. Start checking at 5 minutes and remove each tail as it finishes.

stepSections.title: Garlic-butter pressure-cooked mushrooms
steps: Clean and trim 330 g whole cremini mushrooms. Mince the 3½ cloves of garlic. Put the mushrooms, garlic and a portion of the measured butter in the cooker.
Add water or broth according to the minimum liquid requirement for your cooker. Cook at high pressure for 2 minutes, then quick-release according to the cooker instructions.

With the lid off, use sauté mode to reduce the cooking liquid. If the cooker required extra liquid, spoon some out first. Toss until the mushrooms are glossy and coated. Divide between Jake and Laine using their 180 g and 150 g raw allocations.

stepSections.title: Roasted asparagus
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Trim the tough ends and pat the spears dry. Toss with a little of the measured melted butter, salt and pepper.
Spread in a single layer and roast for 8–12 minutes, checking thin spears first. Pull the pan when the asparagus is bright green and tender-crisp, before switching the oven to broil for the lobster.

stepSections.title: Brown-butter cauliflower mash
steps: Cut 390 g cauliflower into even florets. Steam until very soft, about 12–15 minutes. Drain well and let the excess moisture steam off.
Mash or blend the hot cauliflower with the cream cheese and Parmesan until smooth. Taste and season.
Cook a portion of the measured butter over medium heat, swirling until the milk solids are golden and smell nutty. Take it off the heat immediately and stir it into the mash. Cover and keep warm.

stepSections.title: Chocolate espresso mousse
steps: Make the mousse a few hours ahead. Chop 45 g dark chocolate, melt gently and let it cool until just warm. Brew 35 g espresso and let it cool.
Whip 145 g cold heavy cream with 7 g monk fruit sweetener to soft peaks. Stir the espresso into the chocolate, then whisk in a spoonful of whipped cream to lighten it.
Gently fold the chocolate mixture into the remaining whipped cream. Divide between two ramekins and chill until set, about 2 hours.

stepSections.title: Cooking timeline
steps: At least 2 hours before dinner, make and refrigerate the mousse. Prep the vegetables and lobster tails, then refrigerate the tails until ready to broil.
About 40 minutes before serving, preheat the oven to 425°F and get the cauliflower steaming and the pressure cooker heating. Finish the mash and reduce the mushroom sauce while the other dishes cook.
About 15 minutes before serving, put the asparagus in the oven and begin searing the filets. Check both filets separately and let them rest once they reach temperature.
Pull the asparagus and switch to broil. Cook the lobster while the filets rest, then plate with the warm mash, mushrooms and asparagus. Serve the chilled mousse after dinner.
